recipes.name: Awesome Apple Crisp
ingredients_raw: 2 quarts peeled, cored and sliced apples

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine flour, oatmeal, cinnamon, nutmeg, and brown sugar in a large bowl; cut in butter until mixture is crumbly.
Spoon half of the mixture into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish; pat down with the back of a spoon to form an even layer.
Cover crumb mixture with apple slices, then sprinkle apple slices with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until apples are tender, about 45 to 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Awesome Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: Sweet apple slices are cooked between layers of a delicious crumbly crisp topping made with flour, brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, and oatmeal.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely the best crisp I've ever made. I used about ten medium Cortland apples, which are kind of tart, I added a tsp of vanilla, and I made one and half times the amounts for the crisp part. It totally filled a Pampered Chef 9x13 stoneware dish. This recipe was just wonderful. I served it to company who couldn't get enough, I shared with neighbors who raved, and my family ate it for dessert a couple of nights in a row. Just lucious!! Try this one - you won't be sorry!

Bingo! This recipe works. OK, it’s roughhewn enough for we guys to take a hack at it, here are some guy tricks to cover a variety of Macho Mistakes. You forgot to set out the butter for 10 minutes so it can soften? Recovery: Place the BIG mixing bowl on the stove over the oven that’s heating. That will soften the butter as you mix. Get the BIGGIST whisk you have and use it to knock the chunks of butter down to pea sized bits. Stop mixing at this point. DO NOT pre-melt the butter. DO NOT whisk the butter until you have a smooth mixture. This stops the crisp and makes dough. Recovery: If you do the dough thing, serve with bigger glasses of milk OR use more cream on the dish. HINT: If you serve the dish warm, then put the cream you’re going to pour on it in the microwave on 40% power for 1 minute to knock off the chill. DO NOT boil the cream. More HINTS: (1) Cut slices no finer than about 1/4” thick; it helps them to retain “apple-ness”. (2) After you put the bottom layer of crisp in the baking dish and pour in the apples, PRESS the apples down into the crisp and then press the top layer of crisp dough down into the apples as well. DO NOT crush the apples. The apples will flavor the dough a bit, and there’ll be a better crisp to apple slice ratio as well. (3) DO hold about a ¼ cup of the sugar to pour directly on the apple slices in a bowl and then mix well. (4) DO NOT bake till crust is brown. STOP when apples are tender. Manly Kitchen Mess Rating: No better than 2 out of 10.

I was looking for a "different and hearty" apple crisp and used this one since the oatmeal appealed to me. I only gave it 3 stars because I used the recipe more as a guide since I could tell it needed more. I knew it would be dry as others have stated since nothing is done or added to the apples. The instructions are vague and assume the cook knows exactly what to do. If a beginner followed this recipe I could see a lot of errors happening.

Here are the changes I made: I cut the flower down to 1.5 cups and increased the oats to 2.5 cups. I love cinnamon so I increased it to 1 Tbs. I used the full amount of butter but used it cold cut in 1/2" cubes like you would in pie crust and cut the mix as you would a pie crust to pea size crumble. I used 10 med. apples (considerably more than 2 quarts) and tossed them with 1 Tbs. of lemon juice, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1 Tbs. of cinnamon. I rested the apples to form liquid and strained out the liquid before adding the apples over 1/3 or the crumble slightly packed on the bottom of the baking dish. I whisked 3 Tbs. of corn starch (I would have used tapioca but didn't have any) to the strained liquid and drizzled over the apples before crumbling the remaining 2/3 of the crumble over the top. I baked it longer at 1 hour and rested the crisp for an hour before serving.

It came out AWESOME!! Very juicy thickened sauce. I found my new apple crisp recipe! The family raved and said it was the BEST they ever had!
Outstanding, who ever made the suggestion to go from 2 cups of flour to 1.5 cups couldn't have been more correct.

Very good. I used only 1 cup of flour and increased the oatmeal to 2.5 cup. Also I cooked the apples with 1 cup of sugar and 1 tsp of Cinnamon and thickened with cornstarch after the apples are tender.

This is the first time I've made an apple crisp since home ec in jr high lol. I made it for a potluck dinner and it was delicious! Everyone loved it. I am glad I read through the reviews because I made a few minor revisions. I used 1.5 cups of flour, 1 cup of brown sugar, mixed 1/2 cup pure maple syrup in with the apples (note: I strained the apples before I added them to the pan so I did not pour the liquid in), used a very heaping teaspoon of cinnamon and a heaping 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg. When it was almost done, it looked a little dry on top so I used a fork and "stirred" the topping around a bit then dotted a few very thin slices of butter on it and put it back in the oven. I will definitely make this again!

I loved that this recipe had a double layer of crisp, but I took the flavor profile up to eleven by adding half a teaspoon of ginger and half a teaspoon of all spice (I don’t like nutmeg, so these were substitutions). I also made sure the teaspoon of cinnamon was heaping and added half a teaspoon of kosher salt. It was next level awesome!

I've made this recipe twice now, once as written, and once in an attempt to improve on the original, which isn't as sweet, rich, or flavorful as I would like.

The recipe didn't specify, so I used Granny Smith apples both times, which I consider the default baking apples. I recommend you toss the apples with a bit of white sugar and cinnamon, though, if you're using sweet apples, the sugar probably isn't necessary. 

I recommend slightly increasing the amount of butter and brown sugar in the recipe to 1 3/4 cups of each. This will make the recipe richer and sweeter, but it won't get too crumbly when you cut in the butter, as the mixture will be closer to oatmeal cookie dough, so don't keep mixing expecting crumbly. Also, if you're using unsalted butter, add a teaspoon of salt to the mixture to make it more flavorful.

One more note, base the cooking time exclusively on the apples. Depending on your pan, they might be severely overcooked in 45 minutes, so start checking them early. When the apples are almost done, if you want a crisper topping, turn the oven up to 400 degrees for the last five minutes or so.

Made this today for a group of 15 and served in with homemade cinnamon ice cream. I probably added a bit more nutmeg and cinnamon than was called for, but more of less followed the recipe. I used thick cut oats, along with a mixture of Granny, Green Delicious, and Braeburns. This recipe was easy to make, but needed a deep 9x13 pan, which luckily, I had. i cooked it for an extra 10 minutes since my apples were cut a little thick. At any rate, it was amazing. Best apple crisp recipe. It was not soggy, nor dry. The apples stayed firm and flavorful. everyone absolutely loved it. The addition of cinnamon ice cream was the perfect accompaniment. I will definitely be making this again and keeping this recipe as my permanent go-to for apple crisp.

My grandson requested apple crisp for his dessert the night before he headed off for his junior year in college. I decided to try a different recipe than I normally use and found this one. Everyone loved it! I used 1 1/2 cups flour to the 2 cups of oatmeal, doubled the cinnamon, and omitted the nutmeg. I used a little over 3 quarts (13 cups) of Granny Smith apples. Since Granny's are quite tart I lightly sugared and added cinnamon to the apples. I also doubled the topping recipe because I used more apples and baked it in a 10x15 baking dish.

This was delicious! I only made two small changes. I sprinkled some lemon juice on the apples because I was just using up apples that were in my fridge from apple picking a couple months ago, and I didn't know if the variety I had would be tangy enough. Also, some people said it wasn't sweet enough so I added a couple tablespoons of sugar to the mixture and I added a couple to the apples. I think it would have been good even without the added sugar.
I added C raisins & pecans plus a little apple juice. Also reduced sugar. Turned out real good
I cut nutmeg to 1/8 th teaspoon…first time I made it it had way to much nutmeg, over powered the taste
The apple crisp was incredibly dry.
I have been making this all summer except using fresh peaches. Will switch over to apples for the Fall. I like this better than the cobbler recipes.
It was polished off at a Christmas party.
I followed the recipe but softened the butter in the microwave. It was delicious and a hit for thanksgiving dinner. I used Gravensteins apples which are tart and grow in my yard
